attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the authoritative + forwarding DNS resolver for the 10.100.187.0/24 network shared with node2/node3: it answers `inventory.internal` with node2's address (10.100.187.11) via a VyOS `service dns forwarding authoritative-domain` zone, and forwards all other queries to 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9. node2 and node3 (AlmaLinux) were pointed at node1 for DNS via NetworkManager (dns4=10.100.187.10, dns4_ignore_auto=true). Implementation is an idempotent Ansible playbook (dns.yml) run from node4 (the control node), targeting node1 via the vyos user (sudo/become for VyOS configure-mode commands, since VyOS's config session breaks for non-root non-privileged invocation) and node2/node3 via root, using the community.general.nmcli module. All SSH access was set up using generated/config-managed keys (VyOS pubkey added via `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys`, since manually-appended authorized_keys get wiped by VyOS's own reconciler on commit/reboot). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes (node1, node2, node3, node4): captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health, issued native `reboot`, confirmed disconnection and later reconnection with a changed boot_id, and verified DNS resolution and cluster configuration fully recovered after each restart, including re-running the Ansible playbook cleanly post-restart to confirm idempotency and continued control-plane connectivity.
